title: Normalized algebraic dualizing complexes for quotient local rings
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring and let $\omega\in D(A)$ be a normalized algebraic dualizing complex [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. Let $f:A\twoheadrightarrow B$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with $B\ne0$. Thus $B$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $f(\mathfrak m)$. Then $\omega_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],\omega)$, with its $B$-action induced by $(b\varphi)(x)=\varphi(bx)$ on a derived-Hom representative [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], is a normalized algebraic dualizing complex over $B$ [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing].

proof.text:
Put $I=\ker f$. Since $B
e0$, $I$ is proper and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The element $1_B$ generates $B$ as an $A$-module: every $b$ is $f(a)1_B$. For an ideal $J\subseteq B$, choose finite ideal generators of $f^{-1}J$ in $A$; their images generate $J$ by surjectivity. Thus $B$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The ideal $\mathfrak n=f(\mathfrak m)$ is proper: if $f(a)=1$ with $a\in\mathfrak m$, then $1-a\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. Every $b
otin\mathfrak n$ lifts to $a
otin\mathfrak m$, which is a unit, so $b$ is a unit. Hence $B$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. The map $a+\mathfrak m\mapsto f(a)+\mathfrak n$ identifies $k=A/\mathfrak m$ with $B/\mathfrak n$: it is surjective, and if $f(a)=f(m)$ for $m\in\mathfrak m$, then $a-m\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $a\in\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0A7N, lemma-normalized-quotient, verification that a nonzero quotient is a finite local map as required by Tag 0AX1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-map-dualizing-transfer] to $A\to B$ and $L=\omega$. Step 1 supplies Noetherianity of $B$ and finiteness of $B$ over $A$. The definition [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing] supplies finite cohomology, a bounded injective representative, and the scalar-action isomorphism for $\omega$. The transfer theorem gives precisely these three properties for $\omega_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],\omega)$, with action $(b\varphi)(x)=\varphi(bx)$. Consequently $\omega_B$ is an algebraic dualizing complex over $B$. It remains to check its normalization.

source.place: Tag 0AX1, lemma-normalized-finite, first sentence of proof, invoking Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite.

proof.text: Let $U:D(B)\to D(A)$ be restriction of scalars, and put $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_B(k[0],\omega_B)$, using the residue-field identification of Step 1. Apply the natural derived-Hom isomorphism of [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] with $P=A$, its target ring $B$, $X=k[0]$, and $Y=\omega$. Its coinduced object $C(Y)$ is exactly $\omega_B$, including the prescribed $B$-action. It gives $UT\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(k[0],\omega)\cong k[0]$ in $D(A)$; the second isomorphism is normalization in [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing]. The first comparison is evaluation at $1$, represented by $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(x)(1))$, with inverse $g\mapsto(x\mapsto[b\mapsto g(bx)])$. Thus the comparison uses restriction of scalars and the indicated coinduction, not derived tensor with $B$.

source.place: Tag 0AX1, lemma-normalized-finite, displayed derived-Hom computation; Tag 0A70, lemma-right-adjoint, and Tag 0A71, lemma-RHom-ext.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars keeps the underlying groups, kernels and images of a complex unchanged, so Step 3 gives $H^j(T)=0$ for $j\ne0$ and an $A$-linear isomorphism $\alpha:H^0(T)\to k$. This is $B$-linear: given $b=f(a)$ and $v\in H^0(T)$, one has $\alpha(bv)=\alpha(av)=a\alpha(v)=b\alpha(v)$, and every $b$ has such a lift. Apply [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] in the abelian category of $B$-modules, with $r=0$, to obtain $T\cong H^0(T)[0]\cong k[0]$ in $D(B)$. By [def-per-algebraic-normalized-dualizing], this is the required normalization of the dualizing complex established in Step 2.
